paper.title: Benefits of Monotonicity in Safe Exploration with Gaussian Processes

settings.name_in_paper: Safe sequential maximisation of a function monotone in a safety variable (regret w.r.t. threshold h)
unmapped: Domain D = [0,1] x D_X with D_X subset R^d compact; f is monotonically non-decreasing in the safety variable s
Safety constraint f(s_t,x_t) <= h for all t w.h.p., with h known to the learner
f(0,x) <= h for all x (s=0 always safe) and max f > h
Regret measured against the threshold h: r_t = h - f(s_t,x_t)
settings.definition_quote: We consider the problem of sequentially maximising a fixed but unknown function $f: \mathcal{D} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ over a set of decisions while satisfying safety constraints, where $\mathcal{D} = \mathcal{D_S} \times \mathcal{D_X}$ ... we assume that the function is monotonically increasing in the first argument. ... The algorithm is also required to satisfy the safety constraint $f(s_t, \mathbf{x}_t) \leq h \; \forall t \geq 1$ with high probability. ... $R_T = \sum_{t=1}^T r_t$, where $r_t = h - f(s_t, \mathbf{x}_t)$

settings.name_in_paper: Safe sub-level set estimation of a function monotone in a safety variable
unmapped: Domain D = [0,1] x D_X with D_X subset R^d compact; f monotone non-decreasing in safety variable s
Goal: estimate the h-sub-level set L_h(f) with misclassification loss l_h (infinite penalty for declaring unsafe points safe)
f(0,x) <= h for all x and max f > h; h known
settings.definition_quote: For the sub-level set, we define $L_h(f) = \{(s, \mathbf{x}) \in \mathcal{D} | f(s, \mathbf{x}) \leq h\}$ ... We require that the algorithm should return an $\epsilon$-accurate solution with probability at least $1-\delta$

conditions: d, R and kernel treated as constants
tuning: select points with UCB_{t-1} = h (max s), maximise posterior variance among candidates

source.label: theorem:regret_bound
source.quote: Under the setup and assumptions of Section \ref{sec:problem}, and the choice of $\beta_t$ in Lemma \ref{lemma:beta}, \textsc{\sffamily M-SafeUCB} satisfies the following regret bound with probability at least $1-\delta$: R_T = O\left(B\sqrt{T\gamma_T} + \sqrt{T\gamma_T(\gamma_T + \ln(1/\delta))}\right).

results.notes: Regret is relative to the safety threshold h (r_t = h - f), not to a best action; comparator best_feasible_policy chosen as closest. B (RKHS norm) mapped to S, R to sigma. Algorithm written for discrete D_X but paper claims theory holds for continuous domains. Safety also holds w.p. 1-delta.

conditions: d, R and kernel treated as constants

source.label: theorem:safe_boundary
source.quote: With $l_h(s, \mathbf{x})$ as defined in equation \eqref{eqn:misclassification}, \textsc{\sffamily M-SafeUCB} finds an $\epsilon$-accurate solution $\hat{L}$ with probability at least $1-\delta$: \mathbb{P}\{\max_{s,\mathbf{x} \in \mathcal{D}} l_h(s,\mathbf{x}) \leq \epsilon \} \geq 1-\delta, where \epsilon = O\left(B\sqrt{\gamma_T/T} + \sqrt{(\gamma_T + \ln(1/\delta))\gamma_T/T}\right).

results.notes: Bound is on the maximum misclassification loss epsilon of the returned sub-level set estimate after T rounds (quantity 'other'). Proof gives explicit epsilon = 2 beta_T sqrt(8 gamma_T/T) for T >= 2.
